fileName: Example - ants in the kitchen (new customer).mp3

transcript.text: Thanks for calling Brightside Pest Control, this is Jordan. How can I help you today?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Hi Jordan, I've got ants all over my kitchen counters and I'm kind of at my wit's end.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Oh no, I'm sorry, ants on the counters where you cook is the worst. I can definitely take care of that for you.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: I'm just going to ask you a few questions so I can make sure we get you the right plan, sound good?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Sure.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: When did you first start seeing them, and where do they seem to be coming from?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: About a week ago. They come in under the back door and go straight for the sink. I have two kids and a dog, so I'm worried about sprays.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Totally understand. So it sounds like you want the ants gone fast, and something that's safe around the kids and the dog. Does that sound right?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Great. I'll walk you through our service, and then we'll talk price and get you scheduled if it sounds good.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Your technician will treat the whole foundation outside, so the ants are stopped before they get in. Inside we use pet friendly baits at the back door and under the sink, which take out the colony, not just the ones you see.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Then we come back every three months to keep them out, and if you see any ants in between, we come back for free. Any questions so far?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: No, that sounds good. How much is it?
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Normally the first visit is two hundred ninety nine, but this week we're taking a hundred off for new customers, so it's one ninety nine, and then forty nine a month after that.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Hmm, that's a bit more than I was hoping. Another company quoted me less.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: I hear you, it's smart to compare. If I'm understanding you right, you just want to be sure you're getting real value for the money?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Yeah, pretty much.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: That makes sense. The big difference is we treat the whole yard and foundation every time and come back free in between, so you won't be paying again if they show up. Would Tuesday morning or Thursday afternoon work better for the first visit?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Tuesday morning works.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Perfect. I have you down for Tuesday between eight and ten at 42 Maple Lane. Your technician will call when he's on his way. And if anything else comes up, spiders, wasps, anything, just give us a call first.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Thank you so much for calling in today, we really appreciate your business.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Thank you, bye.
transcript.speaker: customer

outcome.summary: The employee answered the call and explained the ant treatment plan. The customer agreed to the service and scheduled a first visit for Tuesday morning at 42 Maple Lane. The call ended with the appointment booked.

fileName: Example - cancel request, saved with re-service (retention).mp3

transcript.text: Thanks for calling Brightside, this is Priya.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Hi, I'd like to cancel my service please.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Absolutely, I can help you with that. What's the address on the account? Let me just take a quick look here.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: It's 7 Willow Court.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Thank you. I see you've been with us about two years and your last visit was three weeks ago. If you don't mind me asking, how has the service been for you?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: It was fine until this summer, but I keep seeing spiders on the porch and it feels like I'm paying for nothing.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: That makes sense, I'm sorry. So the service was good, but lately you're seeing spiders on the porch and it doesn't feel worth it?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Yes, exactly.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: I totally understand. You've been a loyal customer, so let me offer a couple of options first, and you tell me what you think.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: I can send our lead technician out this week for a free re-service. He'll sweep the webs and treat the porch, eaves and windows really thoroughly, and I'll put a note on your account so the porch gets extra attention every visit. How does that sound?
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Okay, that sounds fair. Let's try that.
transcript.speaker: customer

transcript.text: Great. I have him coming Thursday between one and three. You don't need to be home. Thank you so much for giving us the chance to make it right.
transcript.speaker: employee

transcript.text: Thanks, Priya.
transcript.speaker: customer

outcome.summary: The employee called the customer to address remaining roaches after last treatment. The employee scheduled a free re-service on Monday between 8-10. The call ended with the appointment booked.

items.reason: The employee acknowledged the specific continued roach activity and empathized with the frustration.
items.criteria: Early on, acknowledges the customer's specific reason for calling with genuine empathy (names the actual situation, not a vague 'sorry about that').
items.evidence: I'm sorry you're still seeing them, that's frustrating after a treatment.

items.reason: The employee clearly reassured the customer they would handle it.
items.criteria: Clearly tells the customer they can help and will take care of it, putting the customer at ease (e.g. 'I can definitely take care of this for you').
items.evidence: I'll get this taken care of.

items.reason: The employee did not explain the next step before asking questions.
items.criteria: Before asking questions, tells the customer what happens next (e.g. 'I'm going to ask you a few questions so I can...').

items.reason: The employee asked questions to understand where and what type of roaches were being seen.
items.criteria: Asks questions, mostly open-ended (who, what, when, where, why, how), to understand the situation and its root cause before solving it.
items.evidence: Where are you seeing them, and are they big or small?

items.reason: The employee did not summarize the customer's need in their own terms and check for accuracy.
items.criteria: Repeats back what the customer needs or values in their own terms and checks it's right (e.g. 'So it sounds like you're looking for... does that sound right?').

items.reason: The employee did not set expectations before presenting the solution.
items.criteria: Before presenting the solution, prepares the customer for what's next (e.g. 'I'll walk you through... then we'll get you scheduled').

items.reason: The employee gave a specific re-service plan tailored to the bathroom sink issue.
items.criteria: Explains the solution in specific detail tailored to this customer: what will be done, how, and why it matters for their situation.
items.evidence: I'll send the technician back for a free re-service to put fresh bait under the sink and seal the gaps around the pipes.

items.reason: The employee checked whether the proposed appointment worked for the customer.
items.criteria: Checks the customer agrees or has questions before moving on (e.g. 'Does that work for you?', 'Any questions before we talk price?').
items.evidence: Does Monday morning work?

items.reason: The employee confirmed the appointment was booked.
items.criteria: Asks for the commitment or confirms the action (books the appointment, sets up the change). When the solution has no cost, agreeing to it counts as the close.
items.evidence: You're booked for Monday between eight and ten, no charge.

items.reason: The employee concluded by confirming the appointment window and no charge.
items.criteria: Wraps up loose ends and sets expectations going forward: confirms details such as date and time, address, notes for the technician or what happens next.
items.evidence: You're booked for Monday between eight and ten, no charge.

items.reason: The employee thanked the customer near the end of the call.
items.criteria: Genuinely thanks the customer near the end of the call.
items.evidence: Thanks for letting us know.

items.reason: The employee did not invite the customer to call for other pest needs or questions.
items.criteria: Invites the customer to call for any other pest needs or questions (one-stop shop); on sales calls, mentions the referral program.

coaching.focus: Add an expectation statement before asking questions to set the stage
strengths: Empathized with the customer’s frustration: "I'm sorry you're still seeing them, that's frustrating after a treatment.", "Asked an open‑ended question to gather details: "Where are you seeing them, and are they big or small?", "Provided a clear solution and closed the call: "I'll send the technician back for a free re-service ... Does Monday morning work?"

improvements.point: Add an expectation statement before asking questions to set the stage
improvements.suggestion: I’m going to ask a few questions so I can pinpoint exactly where the roaches are coming from.

improvements.point: Explain why the re‑service is free and what the technician will do
improvements.quote: Seeing a few in the first couple of weeks is normal while the bait works
improvements.suggestion: Because the bait takes a few days to work, we’re offering a free re‑service to ensure the problem is fully addressed.

improvements.point: Ask if there are any other pest concerns before closing
improvements.suggestion: Is there anything else you’re noticing that we should address during the visit?
